'''Grant Lucas Riller''' (born February 8, 1997) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Beijing Royal Fighters]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]] (CBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[College of Charleston Cougars men's basketball|College of Charleston Cougars]].

==High school career==
Riller played basketball for [[Ocoee High School]] in [[Ocoee, Florida]] under head coach Rob Gordon. He was called up to the [[varsity team]] in ninth grade after initially playing at the [[junior varsity team|junior varsity]] level.<ref name="collings">{{cite web |last1=Collings |first1=Buddy |title=Riller hits thriller for Ocoee |url=https://www.pressreader.com/usa/orlando-sentinel/20141127/282338268188340 |website=[[Orlando Sentinel]] |via=[[PressReader]] |access-date=December 2, 2019 |date=November 27, 2014}}</ref> As a senior on December 28, 2014, Riller scored a school-record 53 points in a win over [[Leesburg High School (Leesburg, Florida)|Leesburg High School]] in the finals of the Ocoee Great 8 tournament.<ref name="jackson">{{cite web |last1=Jackson |first1=Emilee |title=Ocoee's Riller scores 53, leads boys hoops to tourney title |url=https://www.orangeobserver.com/article/ocoees-riller-scores-53-leads-boys-hoops-tourney-title |website=[[West Orange Times & Observer]] |access-date=December 2, 2019 |date=December 29, 2014}}</ref> He averaged 29.1 points per game in his senior season.<ref name="miller">{{cite web |last1=Miller |first1=Andrew |title=College of Charleston's Grant Riller to miss season with knee injury |url=https://www.postandcourier.com/sports/college-of-charleston-s-grant-riller-to-miss-season-with/article_f4be9b5a-d8f4-5e3c-872b-becdaaf4d432.html |website=[[The Post and Courier]] |access-date=December 2, 2019 |date=November 2, 2015}}</ref> Riller was deemed a two-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] by [[247Sports.com|247Sports]] and was not rated by [[ESPN]] or [[Rivals.com|Rivals]]. On October 4, 2014, he committed to play college basketball for the College of Charleston over offers from [[Cleveland State Vikings men's basketball|Cleveland State]], [[FIU Panthers men's basketball|FIU]], and [[Hofstra Pride men's basketball|Hofstra]].<ref name="bio">{{cite web |title=Grant Riller |url=https://cofcsports.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/grant-riller/4220 |publisher=College of Charleston Athletics |access-date=December 2, 2019}}</ref>

==College career==
[[File:MBasketball-vs-College of Charleston.jpg|thumb|left|Riller (right) in November 2017]]
Riller suffered a knee injury prior to his freshman season and was forced to redshirt.<ref name="miller" /> He was forced to wear a knee brace despite working all summer to get to full strength. In his collegiate debut, Riller scored 21 points against [[The Citadel Bulldogs basketball|The Citadel]]. He averaged 13.1 points per game as a freshman, second-best on the team.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Miller |first1=Andrew |title=College of Charleston's Grant Riller limping his way to success on basketball court |url=https://www.postandcourier.com/sports/college-of-charleston-s-grant-riller-limping-his-way-to/article_3006a778-e801-11e6-9dd7-2f62f0f8a3ea.html |website=[[The Post and Courier]] |access-date=December 2, 2019 |date=February 3, 2017}}</ref> Riller scored 20 points and added four steals in an 83–76 overtime victory over [[Northeastern Huskies men's basketball|Northeastern]] in the [[Colonial Athletic Association]] Tournament. He was named 2018 CAA Tournament Most Outstanding player and joined teammate [[Joe Chealey]] on the All-CAA First Team. Riller averaged 18.7 points per game as a sophomore.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Ryzewski|first1=Stephen |title=Ocoee High alum Grant Riller leads College of Charleston to NCAA Tournament berth |url=https://www.orangeobserver.com/article/ocoee-high-alum-grant-riller-leads-college-of-charleston-to-ncaa-tournament-berth-observer-preps |website=[[West Orange Times & Observer]] |access-date=December 2, 2019 |date=March 8, 2018}}</ref> He scored a career-high 43 points in a 99–95 loss to [[Hofstra Pride men's basketball|Hofstra]]. As a junior, Riller averaged 21.9 points and 4.1 assists per game and led the Cougars to a 24–9 record.<ref name=preseason>{{cite news |last1=Miller |first1=Andrew |title=College of Charleston's Grant Riller is CAA preseason player of year, Cougars 2nd in poll |url=https://www.postandcourier.com/sports/college-of-charleston-s-grant-riller-is-caa-preseason-player/article_07b0bf92-eab6-11e9-8a9f-330e1f78db23.html |access-date=December 2, 2019 |work=[[The Post and Courier]] |date=October 9, 2019}}</ref> He was again named first-team All-CAA.<ref name="CAA awards">{{cite press release|url=https://caasports.com/news/2019/3/8/hofstras-wright-foreman-repeats-as-caa-mens-basketball-player-of-the-year.aspx |title=Hofstra's Wright-Foreman repeats as CAA men's basketball Player of the Year |publisher=[[Colonial Athletic Association]] |date=March 8, 2019 |access-date=March 8, 2019}}</ref>

Coming into his senior year, Riller was named CAA preseason player of the year.<ref name=preseason/> On December 14, 2019, Riller became the third Cougar in program history to reach the 2,000 career point mark, scoring 21 in a road loss to [[Richmond Spiders men's basketball|Richmond]].<ref>{{cite news|url= 2,000-career point club in loss to Richmond |publisher=[[The Post and Courier]] |date=December 14, 2019 |access-date=December 15, 2019}}</ref> On January 16, 2020, he recorded the first-ever [[double |access-date=January 19, 2020 |date=January 16, 2020}}</ref> At the conclusion of the regular season, Riller was named to the First Team All-CAA.<ref name="CAA awards2">{{cite press ==Professional career==
===Charlotte Hornets (2020–2021)===
On November 18, 2020, Riller was drafted in the second round, 56th overall, in the [[2020 NBA draft]] by the [[Charlotte Hornets]]. On November 30, 2020, he was signed to a [[two-way contract]] by the team. Under the terms of the deal, he split time between the Hornets and their [[NBA G League]] affiliate, the [[Greensboro Swarm]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/press-releases/charlotte-hornets-sign-grant-riller-nate-darling|title=Charlotte Hornets Sign Grant Riller and Nate Darling to Two-Way Contracts|date=November 30, 2020|work=NBA.com|access-date=December 14, 2020}}</ref> He played in 11 G League games, averaging 13.1 points and 3.1 assists per game, and appeared in seven [[National Basketball Association|NBA]] games, averaging 2.6 points and 0.4 assists per game.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Grant Riller, Nate Darling Wrap Up Rookie Seasons as Hornets’ Two-Way NBA Players {{!}} Charlotte Hornets |url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/grant-riller-nate-darling-wrap-rookie-seasons-hornets-two-way-nba-players |access-date=2025-07-01 |website=www.nba.com |language=en}}</ref>

===Delaware Blue Coats (2021)===
On August 30, 2021, Riller signed a two-way contract with the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].<ref>{{cite web|title=76ers Sign Grant Riller to Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/sixers/news/76ers-sign-grant-riller-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=August 30, 2021|access-date=August 30, 2021}}</ref> However, he was waived on December 19 after making four appearances for the [[Delaware Blue Coats]], Philadelphia's affiliate.<ref>{{cite web|title=76ers Sign Myles Powell to Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/sixers/news/76ers-sign-myles-powell-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=December 19, 2021|access-date=December 19, 2021}}</ref>

===Texas Legends (2022–2023)===
On November 3, 2022, Riller was named to the opening night roster of the [[Texas Legends]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/legends-announce-2022-23-opening-night-roster/n-5895504|title=Legends Announce 2022-23 Opening Night Roster|website=oursportscentral.com|date=November 3, 2022|access-date=November 3, 2022}}</ref> Across 26 games he averaged 21.3 points, 3.8 assists, and 2.8 rebounds per game.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-08-21 |title=Grant Riller To Play In China |url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2023/08/grant-riller-to-play-in-china.html |access-date=2025-07-01 |website=Hoops Rumors |language=en-US}}</ref>

=== Beijing Royal Fighters (2023–present) ===
On August 22, 2023, Riller signed to play for the [[Beijing Royal Fighters]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Asian Basketball News, Scores, Stats, Analysis, Standings |url=https://www.asia-basket.com/China/news/825488/Former-players:-Royal-Fighters-sign-Grant-Riller |access-date=2025-07-01 |website=www.asia-basket.com}}</ref> In his first season with the team, Riller averaged 15.6 points, 3.2 rebounds, and 2.6 assists per game in 44 appearances. He improved in his second season, averaging 20.3 points, 4.2 assists, and 3.6 rebounds per game in 43 appearances.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Grant Riller International Stats |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/international/players/grant-riller-1.html |access-date=2025-07-01 |website=Basketball-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>
